[engine] A drift check must test the property whose change it claims to detect, and must separate what is ALLOWED to change from what is not. A check that only tests existence and a check that reddens on every run are both ignored -- the second failure mode is the mirror of the first, and both are cured only by classifying the subject.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-gate-0004 | class: gate-integrity | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

index_assets.py --check printed 'manifest OK: 56 assets, 0 drift' while MANIFEST.jsonl still carried scripts/check/decode_sweep.py at 33992 bytes / mtime 20:52:01 although the file on disk was 38127 bytes / 21:07:40. It only asked os.path.exists per recorded path, so editing any indexed file was invisible. Comparing bytes+mtime surfaced 18 real drifts at once -- but 3 of them were Backup/phase_decomp, Backup/cgc_logs and .workbuddy/memory/2026-09-15.md, i.e. the loop's OWN outputs, which change on every run by design; shipping only that half would have left the check permanently red and therefore trained the reader to ignore it. The fix needed both halves: compare bytes+mtime for source assets, and mark run outputs volatile (existence-only). Verified red-then-green: 18 drifts -> classify -> 12 drifts (the 6 genuine edits stay) -> regenerate -> 0 drifts.
